title: Identifying Bias in Machine-generated Text Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating differences in misclassification rates (human-written essays falsely flagged as machine-generated) between male and female student authors using logistic regression, dominance analysis, and pairwise z-tests for subgroup analysis.

Comparing false positive rates across essays written by White and non-White students, later expanded to six specific racial/ethnic categories, utilizing logistic regression predicting model error, dominance analysis, and z-score significance tests.

Assessing the propensity of detection models to disproportionately misclassify essays written by English-Language Learners (ELL) versus non-ELL students using logistic regression, dominance analysis, and intersectional subgroup analysis.

Analyzing the difference in detection error rates between economically disadvantaged and non-disadvantaged students using performance difference metrics, logistic regression coefficients, and dominance analysis.
